title: Security: Prevent API DoS via unbounded memory read in manifests handler
body:
In `pkg/api/handlers/libpod/manifests.go`, the API endpoint reads the incoming HTTP request payload directly into memory using `io.ReadAll(r.Body)`.

Because there is no upper bound enforced on the reader, a malicious client or a faulty script could send an infinitely streaming or excessively large payload (e.g., several gigabytes) to this endpoint. This forces the Podman daemon to blindly load the entire payload into memory, which can lead to rapid resource exhaustion, an Out-Of-Memory (OOM) crash, and a complete Denial-of-Service (DoS) for the API. 

This can be easily mitigated by wrapping the request body in an `io.LimitReader` to enforce a reasonable maximum manifest size limit before calling `io.ReadAll`. 

I would be happy to submit a quick Pull Request to add an `io.LimitReader` and close this attack vector if maintainers agree!
